The prime-to-p kernel supplies integral elliptic coordinates and the shifted Vélu identity proves integrality of the CM endomorphism. The elliptic torsion product forces a unit coefficient by degree p². Two Frobenius descents identify the exact degree. Frobenius congruences keep the normalized logarithm integral after substitution in its functional equation. The nonidentity tail of the separating period is bounded using disjoint product balls and a spare inverse length at each place. Further inputs include the sigma isogeny identity, the short-vector estimate for choosing the initial cusp-form test point and local multiplicity at the top.

In the common Gram frame, a stabilizer character or an inequivalent unitary type kills each zero-label nonidentity term between different words. Row energies bound the remaining different-word terms. For a single word the positive rank of surviving pairs of flags supplies decay in the weight. The independent dimension count integrates the projection kernel and absorbs the contribution from the deep cusp. Further inputs include counts of arithmetic loops and realized minor labels, the near and far bounds in the dimension count, local representation densities and unit-vector unfolding.

At a split place the two lattice sums and their common-endpoint correction give the spherical Euler quotient. At an inert place triangular row elimination gives the exact length test, the integral row index and trace equation count the admissible rows and corners, and summation over both signs of the outer valuation gives the Euler quotient. The block decomposition counts each coset once. The row–column identity computes the denominator of the last-coordinate ideal. The integral pivot reduction and the existence of the elementary divisors have further local inputs. The real pairing, restricted projection and continuation have separate derivations. The induced spherical function and zonal coefficient have equal finite sums on each double class by their Hecke eigenvalue. The arithmetic vector supplies the eigenvalues. Applying the identity to a self-pair bounds each kernel slice, and rapid decay then makes the mixed triple integral absolutely convergent. The comparison in the standard model matches full-rank Gram fibres and then uses a real-place test and a nonzero scalar on the Fock vacuum to recover the value. For the convergence majorant a dyadic grid covers the unipotent coordinate at each label. Compact relative rational matrices give a separate uniform bound on the number of classes per centre. The exceptional local factors, the global low-rank density identity, the initial row reduction and local Cartan positivity have further inputs.

The cohomological bound uses a common denominator, local divisor estimates, stable cycles, height moments and the two-rate Hecke comparison. Two vertex groups generate a dense subgroup. Its common invariants are constants almost everywhere, so the incidence gap applies to a mean-zero coefficient. In cyclotomic descent the relative ideal degree controls the exponent in the norm and the congruence, while the product of all conjugates gives the field norm. A shortest rational row and two-coordinate approximation give the cusp diagonal bounds. Averaging the independently displaced vertices of a cycle gives its period an ambient L² bound. The partition homotopy and Stokes give a form with the original periods. Averaging over the unit torus preserves those periods. Transporting the mean tensor gives the invariant form whose periods are identified by the two Hecke rates. A mollified Dirichlet polynomial detects a zero and counts exceptional primitive characters. A separate squarefree-character correlation estimate bounds the second moment over candidate primes. The construction on the thick part gives one power of height in the partition derivative. Transfer from the stabilizers computes the complementary share of the lower Hecke bound. Alternating traces give one real functional per complex place on the filtered cycles. The corrected form has a uniform lower bound on both its primal and dual minima. The dual estimate removes small scales by testing a single direction. In the given degree an arithmetic unit separates every positive block weight from one, and the resulting difference bounds in the same general linear group. Transference proceeds by Schur-complement rounding, then the field trace relates the integral dual to the arithmetic one. Deletion and the prism identity show that cup products span the translation cohomology used in the unit argument. Finite residue data give compact representatives on the thick part. The unitary commutant is spanned by place projections and slot permutations, whose cycles become the trace products used to count invariant tests. Column bounds give locally finite overlap, while normalizing the bump on labels gives total weight one on each thick orbit. Integral homological stability explains detection of filtered cycles after increasing matrix size over the same field. Further inputs include connectivity of ordered split sequences, the field-changing comparison, the Artin isomorphism, the relative prime-number theorem and the contour tail for surviving twists.
